items.stem: Distinguish between APC and MPC.
items.answer: APC = C/Y, ratio of total consumption to total income; MPC = ΔC/ΔY, ratio of change in consumption to change in income; APC can exceed 1, MPC lies between 0 and 1.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: APC = C/Y, ratio of total consumption to total income; MPC = ΔC/ΔY, ratio of change in consumption to change in income; APC can exceed 1, MPC lies between 0 and 1.

items.stem: The consumption function of an economy is C = 480 + 0.75Y (₹ crore). Calculate (i) consumption and saving at an income of ₹2,500 crore, and (ii) the break-even level of income.

items.stem: "Saving is negative at low levels of income." Examine this statement with reference to aggregate demand and the consumption function.
items.answer: The statement is valid. People must consume a minimum amount even when income is very low, so consumption exceeds income.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (people must consume a minimum amount even when income is very low, so consumption exceeds income.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: For an economy, C = 590 + 0.75Y and I = 430 (₹ crore). (i) Calculate aggregate demand when income is ₹4,180 crore. (ii) Is the economy in equilibrium at this income? Explain what will happen to inventories and output. (iii) Find the equilibrium income.
items.answer: (i) AD = ₹4,155 crore; (ii) not in equilibrium: output exceeds AD, unplanned inventories pile up, firms reduce output and income falls; (iii) Y = ₹4,080 crore
items.markingKey: (i) AD = 590 + 0.75 × 4180 + 430 = 4155 (1 mark); (ii) AD ≠ Y: output exceeds AD; unplanned inventories pile up; firms reduce output and income falls (2 marks); (iii) Y = (590 + 430) ÷ 0.25 = 4080 (1 mark).

items.stem: "Equilibrium can occur below full employment in the Keynesian model." Examine this statement with reference to ex ante, ex post and equilibrium income.

items.stem: 'An economy in equilibrium must be at full employment.' Do you agree? Explain.
items.answer: No; Keynesian equilibrium is at AD = AS which may be below full employment output (underemployment equilibrium) if effective demand is deficient; full employment needs AD at the full-employment level.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: No; Keynesian equilibrium is at AD = AS which may be below full employment output (underemployment equilibrium) if effective demand is deficient; full employment needs AD at the full-employment level.

items.stem: An increase in investment of ₹900 crore raises national income by ₹1,800 crore. Calculate (i) the multiplier, (ii) MPC, (iii) MPS and (iv) the change in saving.
items.answer: (i) k = 2; (ii) MPC = 0.5; (iii) MPS = 0.5; (iv) ΔS = ₹900 crore
items.markingKey: (i) k = ΔY/ΔI = 1800/900 = 2; (ii) k = 1/(1 − MPC), so MPC = 1 − 1/k = 0.5; (iii) MPS = 1 − MPC = 0.5; (iv) ΔS = MPS × ΔY = 0.5 × 1800 = 900, equal to ΔI at the new equilibrium (1 mark each).

items.stem: Explain the paradox of thrift.
items.answer: If all people save more (MPS rises), consumption and AD fall, income falls by a multiple; at the new equilibrium, total saving equals the unchanged investment, so total saving does not rise; individual virtue becomes a social problem.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: If all people save more (MPS rises), consumption and AD fall, income falls by a multiple; at the new equilibrium, total saving equals the unchanged investment, so total saving does not rise; individual virtue becomes a social problem.

Statement: Ex post saving always equals ex post investment.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Unplanned changes in inventories are counted as investment and make actual investment equal actual saving.
items.markingKey: (b) Unplanned changes in inventories are counted as investment and make actual investment equal actual saving.
options: Output is determined by effective demand, which may be insufficient to employ all resources.
Unplanned changes in inventories are counted as investment and make actual investment equal actual saving.
Output cannot increase further, so the extra demand pushes up prices.
Aggregate demand is then less than aggregate supply, inventories pile up and firms cut production.

items.stem: The following statement about excess and deficient demand is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Excess demand causes unemployment."
items.answer: Excess demand at full employment causes inflation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Excess demand at full employment causes inflation.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: In the study of aggregate demand and the consumption function, the term 'marginal propensity to save' refers to:
items.answer: The change in saving per unit change in income, ΔS/ΔY
items.markingKey: (b) 'marginal propensity to save' means the change in saving per unit change in income, ΔS/ΔY.
options: The consumption that takes place even when income is zero, shown by c̄
The change in saving per unit change in income, ΔS/ΔY
The difference between the value of the security offered and the loan given against it, fixed by the central bank
The level of income at which ex ante aggregate demand equals aggregate supply, or planned saving equals planned investment

items.stem: In an economy, the saving function is S = −130 + 0.2Y and investment is ₹110 crore. The equilibrium level of income is:
items.answer: ₹1,200 crore
options: ₹550 crore
₹240 crore
₹192 crore
₹1,200 crore

items.stem: "Ex post saving always equals ex post investment." Examine this statement with reference to ex ante, ex post and equilibrium income.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Unplanned changes in inventories are counted as investment and make actual investment equal actual saving.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (unplanned changes in inventories are counted as investment and make actual investment equal actual saving.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem:
Statement: An increase in saving by all households may reduce income.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It lowers consumption and aggregate demand, so equilibrium income falls.
items.markingKey: (d) It lowers consumption and aggregate demand, so equilibrium income falls.
options: A larger share of each round of additional income is spent, creating more income in the next round.
Aggregate demand is then less than aggregate supply, inventories pile up and firms cut production.
The income received by factor owners is partly spent, which becomes income for others in successive rounds.
It lowers consumption and aggregate demand, so equilibrium income falls.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Excess demand at full employment causes inflation.
items.answer: Output cannot increase further, so the extra demand pushes up prices.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Output cannot increase further, so the extra demand pushes up prices. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem: The following statement about ex ante, ex post and equilibrium income is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Ex ante saving and ex ante investment are always equal."
items.answer: Only ex post values are always equal; ex ante values are equal only at equilibrium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Only ex post values are always equal; ex ante values are equal only at equilibrium.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: "APC falls as income rises." Examine this statement with reference to aggregate demand and the consumption function.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Consumption increases by less than the increase in income, so the ratio C/Y falls.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (consumption increases by less than the increase in income, so the ratio C/Y falls.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: If the marginal propensity to consume is 0.5, the value of the investment multiplier is:
What is meant by 'paradox of thrift' in the context of the investment multiplier?
items.answer: The result that if all people try to save more, total saving may not increase and income may fall.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: paradox of thrift correctly explained as the result that if all people try to save more, total saving may not increase and income may fall.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about aggregate demand and the consumption function:
I. Investment in the short-run Keynesian model is assumed to be autonomous, i.e. independent of income.
II. Autonomous consumption is positive even at zero income.
III. Saving is negative at income levels below the break-even point.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: II and III only
I and II only
All of them
I and III only

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about excess and deficient demand:
I. Fiscal measures to correct excess demand include higher taxes and lower government expenditure.
II. A deflationary gap causes output, income and employment to fall.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
A policy brief prepared in Jaipur for an imaginary economy says: "Households consume ₹220 crore even at zero income and spend 5/6 of every additional rupee of income. Firms plan an autonomous investment of ₹440 crore." Read the brief and answer the questions.
(i) State the value of the marginal propensity to save. (1)
(ii) Calculate the equilibrium level of income. (1)
(iii) If investment rises by ₹120 crore, calculate the new equilibrium income and explain the role of the multiplier. (2)
items.answer: (i) MPS = 1/6; (ii) Y = ₹3,960 crore; (iii) new Y = ₹4,680 crore (ΔY = 6 × 120 = 720)
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) MPS = 1 − 5/6 = 1/6; (ii) Y = (220 + 440) ÷ (1/6) = 3960; (iii) k = 6, ΔY = 720, new Y = 4680 (1 mark); spending in each round becomes income for others (1 mark).

items.stem: The government wants national income to rise by ₹3,150 crore. If the marginal propensity to save is 1/3, how much additional investment is required? Show your working and state how the multiplier would change if MPS rose.
items.answer: ΔI = ₹1,050 crore (k = 3); a higher MPS would reduce the multiplier
items.markingKey: k = 1 ÷ MPS = 1 ÷ (1/3) = 3 (1 mark); ΔI = ΔY ÷ k = 3150 ÷ 3 = ₹1,050 crore (1 mark); multiplier is inversely related to MPS, so it would fall (1 mark).

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about aggregate demand and the consumption function is NOT correct?
items.answer: MPC can be greater than one.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. MPC lies between zero and one.
options: Consumption rises with income, but by less than the rise in income.
MPC can be greater than one.
Autonomous consumption is positive even at zero income.
Investment in the short-run Keynesian model is assumed to be autonomous, i.e. independent of income.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the investment multiplier:
I. The multiplier and the MPS are inversely related.
II. The multiplier works because one person's spending becomes another person's income.
III. The multiplier also works in reverse, so a fall in investment reduces income by a multiple.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: II and III only
I only
All of them
III only

items.stem: To correct excess demand, the government should:
items.answer: reduce its expenditure
items.markingKey: (c) reduce its expenditure.
options: increase transfer payments
increase its expenditure
reduce its expenditure
reduce taxes

items.stem:
Read the following extract on ex ante, ex post and equilibrium income and answer the questions that follow.
"At equilibrium, planned saving equals planned investment. If aggregate supply exceeds aggregate demand, unplanned inventories accumulate and firms reduce output. In the Keynesian model, equilibrium output can be less than the full-employment output."
(i) If planned saving exceeds planned investment, income will: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'equilibrium income' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Output falls when planned saving exceeds planned investment. (2)
items.answer: (i) fall (ii) The level of income at which ex ante aggregate demand equals aggregate supply, or planned saving equals planned investment. (iii) Aggregate demand is then less than aggregate supply, inventories pile up and firms cut production.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) fall (ii) The level of income at which ex ante aggregate demand equals aggregate supply, or planned saving equals planned investment. (iii) Aggregate demand is then less than aggregate supply, inventories pile up and firms cut production.

items.stem: In an economy, investment increases by ₹1,450 crore and the marginal propensity to consume is 0.5. Calculate (i) the investment multiplier, (ii) the increase in income and (iii) the increase in consumption.
items.answer: (i) k = 2; (ii) ΔY = ₹2,900 crore; (iii) ΔC = ₹1,450 crore

items.stem:
Statement: Equilibrium can occur below full employment in the Keynesian model.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Output is determined by effective demand, which may be insufficient to employ all resources.
items.markingKey: (d) Output is determined by effective demand, which may be insufficient to employ all resources.
options: Aggregate demand is then less than aggregate supply, inventories pile up and firms cut production.
It directly raises aggregate demand, and through the multiplier raises income and employment.
Unplanned changes in inventories are counted as investment and make actual investment equal actual saving.
Output is determined by effective demand, which may be insufficient to employ all resources.
